chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace:

That Ali (peace be upon him) was brought before him two maidservants who had entered the bathhouse, and one of them had bitten the other with her finger, so he ruled that the one who did it should pay her 'uqra (dowry/compensation).

key_terms.اقْتَضَّتْ: She bit (literally: she claimed/demanded with her bite)
key_terms.عُقْرَهَا: Her 'uqra (a specific compensation or dowry paid in cases of injury or breach)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for biting in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the application of 'uqra (often interpreted as a specific monetary compensation or dowry equivalent) in cases of personal injury, specifically biting, within the bathhouse context. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that even minor physical infractions between servants entail financial liability, reflecting the detailed categorization of damages (diya and arsh) in al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam. The ruling serves as a precedent for determining compensation based on the nature of the injury and the status of the parties involved.
